titleEn: The Song of the Cid — Gifts and leave-taking; the Cid tells Ximena of the matches (tiradas 105–108, lines 2131–2189)
part: Tiradas 105–108 · Gifts and leave-taking; the Cid tells Ximena of the matches (lines 2131–2189)

sentences.t:
Yo vos pido merçed a vos, rey natural:
pues que casades mis fijas, así commo a vos plaz,
dad manero a qui las dé, quando vos las tomades;
non gelas daré yo con mi mano, nin de[n]d non se alabarán.”
sentences.l:
I of-you ask favour, of you, king natural:
since that you-marry my daughters, so as to you it-pleases,
give an-agent to one-who them may-give, since you them take;
not to-them-them will-give I with my hand, nor of-it not themselves they-shall-boast.”
sentences.i: “I beg a favour of you, my natural lord and king: since you are giving my daughters in marriage, as it pleases you, name someone to give them away, since it is you who take them; I will not give them with my own hand, nor shall they boast of that.”
sentences.n: Tirada 105 (assonance á, with á-e) — the Çid will not give his daughters away himself; Minaya is to stand for the king (Pidal: El Cid no quiere entregar las hijas por sí mismo.—Minaya será representante del rey). The Çid is still speaking to the king (his speech began at v. 2125): the new assonance runs natural, plaz, tomades, alabarán. rey natural, 'natural king', the lord to whom one is bound by birth. casades, 'you marry (them off)', the -des of the second person plural (= casáis). Pidal's note: dad manero, 'designad un representante' or apoderado, 'name a representative, a proxy' (for dar, compare v. 1405, Dio tres cavalleros, where dar is 'to dispatch, assign', Pidal 'despachó, envió'); more usually one said dar por manero a uno. a qui las dé, 'to one who may give them'. quando, 'since', causal, as at v. 2123. gelas = ge + las, 'them to them': ge is the old form of le/les before a pronoun in l- (modern se las). de[n]d = de + ende, 'of it, thereof'; the n is Pidal's (in italics). With the double negative (non … nin … non): the Infantes shall not be able to boast that the Çid himself put his daughters in their hands.

sentences.t: Respondió el rey: “afé aquí Álbar Fáñez;
sentences.l: Answered the king: “behold here Álbar Fáñez;
sentences.i: The king answered: “Here is Álvar Fáñez;
sentences.n: afé aquí, 'behold here, here is' (afé = he, 'lo, behold', as in afévos, afelos). Álbar Fáñez is Minaya; Pidal accents the Á here and at v. 2140.

sentences.t:
prendellas con vuestras manos e daldas a los ifantes,
assí commo yo las prendo daquent, commo si fosse delant,
sed padrino dellas a tod el velar;
quando vos juntáredes comigo quem digades la verdat.”
sentences.l:
take-them with your hands and give-them to the Infantes,
so as I them take from-here, as if I-were before,
be sponsor of-them at all the veiling;
when you shall-join with-me that-to-me you-tell the truth.”
sentences.i: take them by your hands and give them to the Infantes, just as I take them from here, as though I were there before them; stand as sponsor for them through the whole of the nuptial veiling; and when you are with me again, tell me truly how it went.”
sentences.n: prendellas = prended + las, 'take them', the -d of the imperative assimilated to the pronoun (-dl- > -ll-); daldas = dad + las, 'give them', with the two consonants swapped (-dl- > -ld-): two treatments of the same join. Pidal's note: daquent, 'aquí', 'here'. The king acts out the handing over, taking the daughters by the hands as if he were with them in Valencia, commo si fosse delant; so too the delivery of an inheritance was acted out, as if one were handing over a branch or a turf of it, and Pidal quotes a document of 1297: 'as if we were standing on it, or in a place where we had it in sight'. fosse = fuese, 'I were'; delant, 'present, before (them)'. padrino, 'sponsor', the one who gives the bride away at the ceremony. Pidal's note: el velar, 'la ceremonia de las velaciones', the nuptial veiling, the church blessing of the marriage; tod el = todo el, 'the whole'. juntáredes, future subjunctive, 'when you shall join'. quem = que + me, the enclitic squeeze: 'that you tell me'.

sentences.t: Dixo Álbar Fáñez: “señor, afé que me plaz.”
sentences.l: Said Álbar Fáñez: “lord, behold that me it-pleases.”
sentences.i: Álvar Fáñez said: “My lord, see, I am glad to.”
sentences.n: afé que me plaz, 'see, it pleases me', a courteous yes. plaz = place (plazer, modern placer), the final -e dropped; Tirada 105 ends here.

sentences.t: Tod esto es puesto, sabed, en grand recabdo.
sentences.l: All this is put, know-ye, in great safe-keeping.
sentences.i: All this, be sure of it, is settled with great care.
sentences.n: Tirada 106 (assonance á-o) — the Çid takes leave of the king; gifts (Pidal: El Cid se despide del rey.—Regalos). tod esto = todo esto. sabed, 'know (it)', the narrator's aside to his hearers. recabdo, 'care, good order, security': the arrangement is fast and certain.

sentences.t:
“Ya rey don Alfons, señor tan ondrado,
destas vistas que oviemos, de mí tomedes algo.
sentences.l:
“O king don Alfons, lord so honoured,
of-these meeting that we-had, from me take something.
sentences.i: “King Don Alfonso, lord so honoured, in token of this meeting we have held, take something from me.
sentences.n: The speaker is the Çid, not named: the poem often lets a speech begin with no verb of saying. ya, the vocative 'O', as in ya Campeador. vistas, 'meeting', plural in form. oviemos, 'we had', preterite of aver. tomedes, present subjunctive as a polite command, 'may you take'. algo, 'something', here 'a gift'.

sentences.i: I have brought you thirty palfreys, well fitted out, and thirty swift horses, well saddled; take these, and I kiss your hands.”
sentences.n: Tráyovos = trayo + vos, 'I bring you' (trayo = traigo). [treínta]: the first 'thirty' is Pidal's, in italics; the next line has the manuscript's own. Pidal accents treínta in both lines, keeping its old three syllables. palafrés, 'palfreys', easy-paced riding horses; cavallos corredores, 'running horses', swift war-horses. estos, 'these', picks up the noun: 'these well fitted out'. aquesto = esto. beso vuestras manos, the vassal's formal thanks.

sentences.t:
Dixo el rey don Alfons: “mucho me avedes enbargado.
Reçibo este don que me avedes mandado;
sentences.l:
Said the king don Alfons: “much me you-have burdened.
I-receive this gift that to-me you-have granted;
sentences.i: King Alfonso said: “You overwhelm me with kindness. I receive this gift you have granted me;
sentences.n: Pidal's note: embargado (printed enbargado in the text), 'abrumado', 'weighed down' by so many attentions. Pidal's note to 2148: que me avedes mandado, 'que me habéis otorgado', 'that you have granted me': mandar here 'to offer, bestow', not 'command'. avedes = habéis.

sentences.t:
plega al Criador, con todos los sos santos,
este plazer quem feches que bien sea galardonado.
sentences.l:
may-it-please the Creator, with all the his saints,
this pleasure that-to-me you-do that well it-be rewarded.
sentences.i: may it please the Creator, with all his saints, that this kindness you do me be well rewarded.
sentences.n: plega, present subjunctive of plazer, 'may it please'. los sos santos, article + possessive, 'his saints' (sos = sus). plazer, 'pleasure, kindness done'. quem = que + me again. feches = fazedes, 'you do'. que bien sea galardonado, 'that it be well rewarded': que picks up the wish after the long object set first.

sentences.i: My Çid Ruy Díaz, you have done me great honour; I am well served by you, and I count myself repaid; while I yet live, may you have something from me!
sentences.n: R[o]y, only the o in italics (Pidal's restoration); Diaz unaccented as printed. so = soy. Pidal's note: tengon, 'téngome', 'I hold myself': the enclitic me cut to -m and written n. por pagado, 'as paid, satisfied'. se[d]iendo, gerund of seer, 'to be' (= siendo), the d Pidal's: aun bivo sediendo, 'being still alive'. ayades, present subjunctive of aver, 'may you have'; compare v. 205, aun vea el dia que de mí ayades algo, the Çid's own wish to Martín Antolínez.

sentences.t:
A Dios vos acomiendo, destas vistas me parto.
Afé Dios del çielo, que lo ponga en buen [recabdo]!”
sentences.l:
To God you I-commend, from-these meeting myself I-part.
Behold God of-the heaven, that it he-put in good [keeping]!”
sentences.i: I commend you to God; I take my leave of this meeting. May God in heaven bring it all to good issue!”
sentences.n: acomiendo, 'I commend' (acomendar). me parto, 'I depart'. afé, 'behold', here hardly more than an exclamation: 'there is God in heaven, may he…'. [recabdo]: the word is Pidal's, in italics (the ! is italic too), echoing recabdo at v. 2141; poner en buen recabdo, 'to set in good order, bring to a safe end'. Tirada 106 ends here.

sentences.t: Sobrel so cavallo Bavieca mio Çid salto di[o]:
sentences.l: Upon-the his horse Bavieca my Çid leap gave:
sentences.i: My Çid leapt up onto his horse Babieca:
sentences.n: Tirada 107 (assonance ó, with ó-e) — many of the king's men go with the Çid to Valencia; the Infantes are given Per Vermudoz as escort (Pidal: Muchos del rey se van con el Cid a Valencia. Los infantes acompañados por Pedro Vermúdez). Pidal prints vv. 2127–2130 here, after the rubric and before v. 2156, keeping their numbers: the numbers show they stood after v. 2126, in the middle of the Çid's reply to the king; we follow his print order. His note on these pages gives no reason. sobrel = sobre + el, 'upon the'. salto dio, 'gave a leap', 'sprang'; di[o], only the o Pidal's.

sentences.t:
“Aquí lo digo, ante mio señor el rey Alfons:
qui quiere ir a las bodas, o reçebir mi[o] don,
daquend vaya comigo; cuedo quel avrá pro.”
sentences.l:
“Here it I-say, before my lord the king Alfons:
who wishes to-go to the weddings, or receive my gift,
from-here let-him-go with-me; I-think that-to-him it-will-have profit.”
sentences.i: “I say it here, before my lord King Alfonso: whoever wishes to come to the weddings, or to receive a gift from me, let him come with me from here; I think it will be to his profit.”
sentences.n: qui, 'whoever'. mi[o], the o Pidal's. daquend = de + aquend(e), 'from here, from this side'. cuedo = cuido, 'I think, I believe'. quel = que + le, 'that to him'; avrá pro, 'there will be profit' (pro, 'advantage').

sentences.t:
Yas espidió mio Çid de so señor Alfons,
non quiere quel escurra, dessí luégo[l] quitó.
sentences.l:
Now-himself took-leave my Çid of his lord Alfons,
not he-wants that-him he-escort, thereupon at-once-him he-left.
sentences.i: Now my Çid took his leave of his lord Alfonso; he would not have the king escort him on his way, and there and then he parted from him.
sentences.n: Yas = ya + se. espidió, 'took leave' (espedirse = despedirse). Pidal's note: 'no quiere que salga a despedirle (v. 1067), allí mismo se separó de él', 'he does not want him to come out to see him off; right there he parted from him'. escurrir, 'to escort a parting guest some way on the road'; quel = que + le. dessí = des + í, 'from there, thereupon'. luégo[l] = luego + le, 'at once … from him', the l Pidal's. quitó, 'he parted'.

sentences.t:
Veriedes cavalleros, que bien andantes son,
besar las manos, espedirse de rey Alfons:
sentences.l:
You-would-see knights, who well faring are,
kiss the hands, take-leave of king Alfons:
sentences.i: You might have seen knights, men of good fortune, kissing the king's hands and taking their leave of King Alfonso:
sentences.n: Veriedes, 'you would see', conditional of ver: the singer's appeal to his hearers. bien andantes, 'well-faring, fortunate'. de rey Alfons, without the article, as often with rey before a name.

sentences.t:
“Merçed vos sea e fazednos este perdón:
hiremos en poder de mio Çid a Valençia la mayor;
seremos a las bodas d' ifantes de Carrión
he de fijas de mio Çid, de don Elvira e doña Sol.”
sentences.l:
“Favour to-you be and do-us this pardon:
we-will-go in power of my Çid to Valençia the great;
we-will-be at the weddings of Infantes of Carrión
and of daughters of my Çid, of don Elvira and doña Sol.”
sentences.i: “Of your grace, forgive us this: we shall go in my Çid's following to Valencia the great; we shall be at the weddings of the Infantes of Carrión and the daughters of my Çid, Doña Elvira and Doña Sol.”
sentences.n: Merçed vos sea, 'be it your grace', 'if you please'. Pidal's note: fazednos este perdón, 'perdonadnos esto', 'forgive us this' (fazed = haced, f- for h-). hiremos = iremos, the h- only a spelling, as in he 'and' (= e) in the last line. en poder de, 'in the power of, under the command of'. Valençia la mayor, 'Valencia the great'. d' ifantes = de ifantes, the vowel elided, ifantes as usual without the article. Carrión: the print has 'Carrióu', a turned n, read Carrión; the line has no closing punctuation, as printed. don Elvira, so printed (don, not doña), as at vv. 2088, 2097; 'Doña Elvira' in the English.

sentences.i: This pleased the king, and he let them all go; the Çid's company grows and the king's grew less; great are the numbers going with the Campeador.
sentences.n: plogo, preterite of plazer, 'it pleased'. Pidal's note: soltó, 'dejó marchar libremente', 'let them go freely' (compare v. 1400). creçe … mengó, present beside preterite, the epic tense-mixing; mengó = menguó, 'dwindled'. yentes = gentes. Canpeador: so printed here, with n.

sentences.t: Adeliñan pora Valençia, la que en buen punto ganó.
sentences.l: They-make-straight for Valençia, the-one that in good moment he-won.
sentences.i: They make their way to Valencia, which he won in a happy hour.
sentences.n: adeliñar, 'to make straight for'. pora = para. en buen punto, 'at a good moment', a cousin of the en buen ora formula: 'in a happy hour'.

sentences.t:
A Fernando e a Di[a]go aguardar los mandó
a Per Vermu[doz] e Muño Gustioz,
—en casa de mio Çid non a dos mejores,—
que sopiessen s[u]s mañas d' ifantes de Carrión.
sentences.l:
To Fernando and to Di[a]go to-attend them he-ordered
to Per Vermu[doz] and Muño Gustioz,
—in house of my Çid not there-are two better,—
that they-might-know their ways of-the Infantes of Carrión.
sentences.i: He charged Per Vermudoz and Muño Gustioz to attend on Fernando and Diego — in my Çid's household there are no two better men — so that they might learn the ways of the Infantes of Carrión.
sentences.n: The order of words: mandó a Per Vermudoz e Muño Gustioz aguardar a Fernando e a Diago, 'he ordered P. V. and M. G. to attend Fernando and Diego'; the los of the first line takes up the Infantes again. Pidal's note: aguardar, 'servir, acompañar', 'to serve, accompany' (v. 1449); but they are also to watch them. Di[a]go, the a Pidal's; Vermu[doz], the ending his. non a = no ha, 'there are not' (aver impersonal). sopiessen = supiesen, 'might know'. s[u]s, the u Pidal's; sus mañas d' ifantes, 'their ways, of the Infantes', the possessive taken up by de. mañas, 'habits, character'.

sentences.t:
E va i A[n]su[o]r Gonçál[v]ez, que era bullidor,
que es largo de lengua, mas en lo al non es tan pro.
sentences.l:
And goes there A[n]su[o]r Gonçál[v]ez, who was a-bustler,
who is long of tongue, but in the other not is so worthy.
sentences.i: And with them goes Asur González, a noisy fellow, long of tongue but in all else of little worth.
sentences.n: i = 'there' (y). A[n]su[o]r Gonçál[v]ez: the n, the o and the v are Pidal's. Pidal's note: bullidor, 'bullanguero', 'rowdy, a stirrer'; this Asur González was the elder brother of the Infantes of Carrión: though the poet does not say so, the hearers would know at once from the surname that he was a brother of Diego and Fernando. 'Asur González' in the English is Pidal's modern form of the name. largo de lengua, 'long of tongue', a loose talker. lo al, 'the rest, anything else'. pro, here an adjective, 'worthy, valiant'.

sentences.t: Grant ondra les dan a ifantes de Carrión.
sentences.l: Great honour to-them they-give to Infantes of Carrión.
sentences.i: Great honour is done to the Infantes of Carrión.
sentences.n: les … a ifantes, the pronoun and the noun together, 'to them, to the Infantes', ifantes without the article as at vv. 2162, 2171, 2178. ondra = honra, 'honour'.

sentences.t:
Afelos en Valençia, la que mio Çid gañó;
quando a ella assomaron, los gozos son mayores.
sentences.l:
Behold-them in Valençia, the-one that my Çid won;
when to it they-came-in-sight, the joys are greater.
sentences.i: See them now in Valencia, the city my Çid won; when they came in sight of it, the rejoicing grew greater still.
sentences.n: Afelos = afé + los, 'behold them', the narrator pointing. gañó, 'won', a form beside ganó (v. 2167). assomar, 'to come into view (over a rise)'. son mayores, 'are greater', tense-mixing again.

sentences.t:
Dixo mio Çid a don Pero e a Muño Gustioz:
“Dad les un reyal a ifantes de Carrión,
[e] vos con ellos se[e]d, que assí vos lo mando yo.
sentences.l:
Said my Çid to don Pero and to Muño Gustioz:
“Give to-them a lodging to Infantes of Carrión,
[and] you with them be, for thus you it command I.
sentences.i: My Çid said to Don Pero and to Muño Gustioz: “Give the Infantes of Carrión quarters of their own, and stay with them yourselves, for so I command you.
sentences.n: don Pero is Per Vermudoz. Pidal's note: reyal, 'real, albergue', 'quarters, lodging' (the word for a camp or royal quarters). Dad les … a ifantes, the pronoun taken up by the noun. [e], the word Pidal's; se[e]d, imperative of seer, 'be' (= sed), the second e Pidal's.

sentences.t:
Quando viniere la mañana, que apuntare el sol,
verán a sus esposas, a don Elvira e a doña Sol.”
sentences.l:
When shall-come the morning, when shall-break the sun,
they-will-see to their brides, to don Elvira and to doña Sol.”
sentences.i: When the morning comes and the sun breaks, they shall see their brides, Doña Elvira and Doña Sol.”
sentences.n: viniere, apuntare, future subjunctives in the time clause, 'when (it) shall come … shall dawn'. que, 'when'. esposas, 'betrothed, brides'; a sus esposas, the personal a before a human object. don Elvira again so printed. Tirada 107 ends here.

sentences.i: That night they all went to their lodgings; my Çid the Campeador went into the citadel, and Doña Ximena and both her daughters received him:
sentences.n: Tirada 108 (assonance á-a) — the Çid tells Ximena of the marriage (Pidal: El Cid anuncia a Jimena el casamiento). f[o]ron = fueron, the o Pidal's. posadas, 'lodgings'. alcáç[er], 'citadel, fortress', the er Pidal's. reçibiólo = reçibió + lo. amas = ambas, 'both'.

sentences.t:
“¿Venides, Campeador, buena çinxiestes espada!
muchos dias vos veamos con los ojos de las caras!”
sentences.l:
“Come-you, Campeador, (in) a-good (hour) you-girded sword!
many days you may-we-see with the eyes of the faces!”
sentences.i: “So you are come, Campeador — in a good hour you girded on your sword! May we see you for many days with the eyes of our faces!”
sentences.n: Pidal's note: para la interrogación de saludo, v. 204: the greeting put as a question, ¿Venides…, 'are you come?', as when the Çid welcomed Martín Antolínez; Pidal opens it with ¿ and closes it with !, as printed. buena çinxiestes espada, the en buen ora formula, 'in a good hour you girded on your sword', with both en and ora left unsaid: buena (printed whole, in roman) stands for buen(a) ora, as in en buen[a] çinxiestes espada at vv. 41, 175 and 1706, and does not go with espada. çinxiestes, preterite of çeñir, 'to gird'. veamos, present subjunctive as a wish. con los ojos de las caras, 'with the eyes of our faces', a stock fullness; dias unaccented as printed.

sentences.i: “Thanks be to the Creator, I am come, my honoured wife! I bring you sons-in-law who will bring us honour; thank me for it, my daughters, for I have married you well!”
sentences.n: mugier = mujer, 'wife'. Pidal's note: vos adugo, 'os traigo', 'I bring you' (aduzir). de que, 'from whom', referring to persons. ondrança, 'honour'. gradídmelo = gradid + me + lo, 'thank me for it'. ca, 'for'. vos he casadas, 'I have you married': the participle agrees with the object vos, the daughters (aver still close to 'hold'). This is the first the poem shows Ximena hearing of the matches.
